name: Ginkgo Bioworks
short_description: Programs cells like code at industrial scale for biosecurity and biopharma.
why_relevant: The largest open cellular engineering foundry in the world.
history: Founded in 2008 by MIT scientist Tom Knight and his students, Ginkgo grew out of MIT's synthetic-biology community as a 'foundry' that programs cells like code. It expanded through acquisitions including Gen9 in 2017 and Zymergen in 2022, and scaled during the COVID-19 pandemic with large surveillance-testing contracts. In 2021 it went public via a SPAC backed by major investors. Today Ginkgo operates the world's largest open cellular engineering platform, serving biopharma, agriculture, and biosecurity clients across its Cell Programming and Biosecurity segments.

name: Twist Bioscience
short_description: Silicon-based DNA synthesis powering next-generation sequencing and engineered antibodies.
why_relevant: Commoditized synthetic DNA at scale for research and GMP.
history: Founded in 2013, Twist set out to miniaturize DNA synthesis on silicon wafers, printing thousands of novel DNA strands on a single chip. It launched commercial synthetic DNA products, then expanded into next-generation sequencing target enrichment and antibody discovery. The company went public on the Nasdaq in 2018 and later added GMP manufacturing for therapeutic and clinical use. Twist also partnered with Microsoft on DNA-based digital storage. Today it is a leading industrial-scale supplier of synthetic DNA, RNA, and antibodies for research and biopharma worldwide.

name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
short_description: Uses automated lab experiments and machine learning to discover drugs.
why_relevant: Pioneered map-of-biology scale screening with AI.
history: Founded in 2013 by Christopher Gibson and colleagues, Recursion began running automated, hypothesis-free experiments in a basement lab, generating massive cell-imaging datasets. It went public on the Nasdaq in 2021 and acquired the AI companies Cyclica and Valence Labs in 2022-2023, then partnered with Nvidia in 2024 to build large biological foundation models. Its disease-agnostic platform has produced multiple clinical candidates advanced with partners such as Bayer and Roche/Genentech. Today Recursion combines high-throughput phenomics with machine learning at an industrial scale.

name: Insilico Medicine
short_description: End-to-end generative AI platform for target discovery and drug design.
why_relevant: First AI-discovered drug to enter human trials in fibrosis.
history: Founded in 2014 by Alex Zhavoronkov, Insilico built one of the first end-to-end generative AI platforms spanning target discovery, generative chemistry, and clinical prediction. Its AI-designed candidate for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis became the first such drug to enter human clinical trials in 2021 and posted positive Phase 2a topline data in 2024. Backed by investors including Warburg Pincus and Qiming Venture Partners, the company has signed billion-dollar licensing deals with major pharma. It now advances a pipeline of AI-generated medicines toward approval.

name: Cradle Bio
short_description: Generative AI to design and optimize proteins for speed.
why_relevant: Brief was to make protein engineering as easy as prompting.
history: Founded in 2021 in the Netherlands by former Google executive Stef van Grieken and protein engineers, Cradle emerged to make protein engineering as easy as prompting an AI. The company raised a Series A led by Index Ventures in 2023 and expanded its investor base across Europe and the United States. Its generative AI platform uses wet-lab feedback so models continuously learn from real experiments. Cradle's technology helps customers design enzymes and antibodies faster while improving key protein properties, serving a growing set of industrial and biopharma partners.

name: Profluent
short_description: Generates novel proteins for gene editing, including the OpenCRISPR-1 editor.
why_relevant: Open-sourced an AI-designed gene editor as a public asset.
history: Founded in 2022 by Ali Madani, an AI researcher who previously led protein language-model work behind ProGen, Profluent set out to apply large language models to protein invention. The company attracted leading computational and wet-lab talent and raised tens of millions of dollars, including a 2024 round led by Insight Partners and Air Street Capital. In 2024 it open-sourced OpenCRISPR-1, an AI-designed gene editor built on the Cas9 architecture, published as a freely available public asset. Profluent continues developing generative protein models for gene editing and therapeutic biologics.

name: Generate:Biomedicines
short_description: Uses generative AI to create de novo programmable medicines.
why_relevant: De novo protein therapeutics designed computationally and wet-lab validated.
history: Founded in 2018 by Flagship Pioneering, Generate:Biomedicines built a generative biology platform that designs de novo proteins from scratch rather than modifying nature's originals. It secured major funding rounds, including $273 million in 2020 and $370 million in 2021, and formed a multi-program collaboration with Novartis in 2022 valued at up to $1.5 billion. The company opened its own GMP manufacturing facility to produce computationally designed biologics. Its platform now feeds a pipeline spanning oncology, immunology, and rare disease, with multiple candidates moving toward the clinic.

name: AbCellera
short_description: Single-cell antibody discovery that helped create COVID-19 antibodies.
why_relevant: Rapid pandemic antibody development proved its discovery platform.
history: Founded in 2012 out of the University of British Columbia by microfluidics researcher Carl Hansen, AbCellera built a single-cell platform that interrogates millions of antibody-producing cells. The platform rose to prominence in 2020 when its COVID-19 collaboration with Eli Lilly produced the antibody bamlanivimab in record time. That success fueled an oversubscribed Nasdaq IPO in December 2020, raising more than half a billion dollars. AbCellera has since signed discovery partnerships across major pharma and grown an internal therapeutic pipeline.

name: Mammoth Biosciences
short_description: Builds CRISPR-based detection systems co-founded by Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna.
why_relevant: Cell-free CRISPR sensors for point-of-care testing.
history: Founded in 2017 by Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and colleagues Janice Chen, Lucas Harrington, and Trevor Martin, Mammoth builds CRISPR detection systems based on the enzyme Cas13. During the COVID-19 pandemic it rapidly developed point-of-care CRISPR tests for SARS-CoV-2, including collaborations with UCSF. The company raised more than $150 million, including a Series D in 2021, and has disclosed partnerships with major biopharma such as GSK. Today Mammoth focuses on fast, low-cost CRISPR diagnostics for infectious disease and beyond.

name: Caribou Biosciences
short_description: Uses CRISPR genome editing to develop off-the-shelf cell therapies.
why_relevant: Allogenic CAR-T candidates built with precise CRISPR insertion.
history: Founded in 2011 as a spinout from Jennifer Doudna's Berkeley laboratory, Caribou developed precise CRISPR-Cas9 editing tools and later built its chRDNA architecture for cell therapy. Its allogeneic CAR-T candidates, led by CB-010, advanced through Phase 1 clinical trials, while a 2021 collaboration with AbbVie validated its approach. The company listed on the Nasdaq in 2021 and raised significant funding for its pipeline. Today Caribou focuses on developing off-the-shelf CRISPR-engineered cell therapies, positioning itself as a leader in allogeneic CAR-T built with precise CRISPR insertion.

name: BenevolentAI
short_description: Uses a knowledge graph and AI to find new treatments from vast literature.
why_relevant: Exemplar of combining causal biomedical reasoning with AI.
history: Founded in London by Ken Mulvany, Ivan Griffin, and Jacqueline Hunter, BenevolentAI built a biomedical knowledge graph spanning scientific literature, patents, and clinical data. It conducted early COVID-19 drug-repurposing analyses and listed on Euronext Amsterdam in 2022 after a SPAC combination. The company strengthened its AI platform through acquisition, and collaborations with partners including AstraZeneca and Merck KGaA. BenevolentAI continues to apply causal AI reasoning and machine learning to accelerate drug discovery and development.

name: Tempus
short_description: Collects clinical and molecular data to guide AI-driven care decisions.
why_relevant: Built the largest real-world molecular dataset in oncology.
history: Founded in 2015 by Eric Lefkofsky in Chicago, Tempus has assembled one of the largest collections of clinical and molecular oncology data in the world. The company expanded across testing, trials, and AI-driven analytics, and went public on the Nasdaq in 2021. It built large health-system collaborations and expanded into clinical trial matching and drug development. Today Tempus uses its real-world molecular dataset to guide AI-assisted care decisions for cancer patients and health systems nationwide.

name: Grail
short_description: Develops a blood test to detect multiple cancers at early stages.
why_relevant: Galleri multi-cancer early detection is a billion-dollar bet on screening.
history: Founded in 2016 as a spinout of Illumina, Grail set out to detect cancer early from a simple blood test. Its Galleri test uses DNA methylation patterns to screen for multiple cancer types, and clinical trials like PATHFINDER showed detection of hard-to-find and early-stage cancers. Grail returned to Illumina ownership in 2021, and Illumina later divested it in 2024 under regulatory pressure. Grail now continues advancing multi-cancer early detection, with long-term interventional studies underway and expanding access to its Galleri test.

name: Freenome
short_description: Detects cancer from blood using machine learning on cell-free features.
why_relevant: Validating pan-cancer screening from a single blood draw.
history: Founded in 2014, Freenome develops pan-cancer blood screening combining cell-free DNA analysis with machine learning and AI-trained classifiers. The company has raised over $400 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Roche, validating its approach in large studies. Freenome's technology analyzes multiple molecular features from a single blood draw and has shown strong performance in detecting early and late-stage cancers. It is now preparing regulatory submissions while expanding research collaborations across major clinical networks.

name: Guardant Health
short_description: Companion diagnostics and early cancer detection from blood.
why_relevant: Widely reimbursed liquid biopsy used across oncology clinics.
history: Founded in 2011, Guardant Health pioneered liquid biopsy from a simple blood draw using PCR and sequencing-based profiling. Its Guardant360 test became one of the most widely used and reimbursed genomic profiling tools in oncology, and it expanded into early cancer detection with the Shield platform. The company went public in 2018 and has since launched large screening studies and companion diagnostics. Today Guardant supports genomic-informed care and multi-cancer screening for clinics around the world.

name: Color Health
short_description: Population-scale genomic screening integrated with primary care.
why_relevant: Makes hereditary cancer risk screening a routine preventive tool.
history: Founded in 2013, Color began as a consumer genetics company offering low-cost hereditary cancer testing. It partnered with large employers and health systems, adding population-scale programs in cardiology and pharmacogenetics. Color rose to prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic, building testing infrastructure that reached millions of people. Today the company focuses on population genomics integrated with primary care, helping clinics deliver routine hereditary-risk screening as part of standard preventive medicine.

name: Helix
short_description: Large-scale genomic sequencing platform feeding many consumer products.
why_relevant: Sequencing-as-a-service model behind dozens of health brands.
history: Founded in 2015, Helix built an end-to-end population genomics platform that sequences exomes and offers launchable health products through partners. The company operates large sequencing infrastructure and works with health systems, employers, and public health programs on population-scale initiatives. Helix has sequenced hundreds of thousands of people and developed an Exome+ product plus partnerships in chronic-disease screening. Its sequencing-as-a-service model drives dozens of consumer health brands and makes genomics routine in preventive care.

name: Genome Medical
short_description: Telehealth network of genetics experts for ordering and explaining tests.
why_relevant: Solves the clinician shortage for interpreting genomic results.
history: Founded in 2016, Genome Medical built a telemedicine network of genetics experts to help patients order, interpret, and act on genomic tests. The company integrated with health systems, laboratories, and care teams to deliver remote genetic counseling at scale. It expanded into hereditary cancer and cardiology programs and developed technology to streamline variant interpretation. Today Genome Medical addresses the shortage of genetics clinicians by pairing telehealth consultations with tools that help clinics deliver genomic medicine more efficiently.

name: Sophia Genetics
short_description: Cloud platform standardizing genomics interpretation across hospitals.
why_relevant: Democratic access to federated genomic analytics for hospitals.
history: Founded in 2011 in Switzerland, Sophia Genetics created a cloud analytics platform that standardizes genomic data interpretation across hospitals. The company went public on the Nasdaq in 2021 and deployed its SOPHiA DDM platform across hundreds of institutions worldwide. It invests heavily in research collaborations and applies AI to oncology and rare-disease testing at scale. Today Sophia Genetics continues to democratize access to federated genomics analytics, processing millions of genomic profiles each year through a global data network.

name: Delve Bio
short_description: Identifies hard-to-find pathogens from sequencing of body fluids.
why_relevant: Aims to end diagnostic odysseys for mysterious infections.
history: Founded in 2019 as a spinout of the University of California, San Francisco, Delve Bio works on metagenomic sequencing to identify hard-to-find pathogens from body fluids. The company developed a stringent diagnostics laboratory and an AI-based classification engine for clinical results. In 2024 it announced a partnership with Roche Diagnostics to help laboratories adopt metagenomic next-generation sequencing at scale. Today Delve Bio aims to end long diagnostic odysseys for mysterious infections and broaden access to metagenomic NGS diagnostics.

name: Arcturus Therapeutics
short_description: Develops mRNA and self-amplifying RNA medicines and vaccines.
why_relevant: Showed mRNA vaccines can be thermostable for low-resource settings.
history: Founded in 2013, Arcturus developed mRNA and self-amplifying RNA medicines using its LUNAR lipid nanoparticle delivery platform. The company advanced its COVID-19 vaccine candidate in Japan through a partnership with CSL and Daiichi Sankyo and showed that mRNA vaccines can be thermostable for low-resource settings. It has also branched into liver-targeted therapies and genetic diseases. Arcturus continues to develop RNA vaccines and therapeutics for infectious disease, rare disease, and beyond.

name: Moderna
short_description: The mRNA pioneer behind the first widely deployed mRNA vaccine.
why_relevant: Proved the mRNA platform category and now targets cancer and rare disease.
history: Founded in 2010 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Moderna pioneered the mRNA-LNP platform for human therapeutics. In 2020-2021 its Spikevax vaccine became one of the first mRNA vaccines authorized for COVID-19, deployed to billions of people worldwide and generating tens of billions in revenue. Moderna expanded its pipeline across respiratory vaccines, cancer, rare disease, and latent-virus programs. Today the company is applying the platform to personalized cancer vaccines and other mRNA-based medicines while building global manufacturing capacity.

name: CureVac
short_description: German mRNA developer focused on cancer and infectious disease vaccines.
why_relevant: Long-standing European counterweight in the mRNA technology race.
history: Founded in 2000 in Tübingen, Germany, CureVac has spent over two decades developing mRNA technology, including unmodified RNA and optimized codon design. It partnered with GSK on next-generation vaccines, introduced candidates like CV2CoV, and maintains a pipeline of infectious-disease and cancer vaccines. The company listed on the Nasdaq in 2020 and continues to advance thermostable mRNA approaches on its proprietary platform. Today CureVac remains a leading European challenger in the global mRNA race.

name: Absci
short_description: Computationally designs and validates antibodies with wet-lab feedback.
why_relevant: De novo antibody candidates designed in silico and tested in weeks.
history: Founded in 2020, Absci develops de novo antibody discovery using zero-shot generative AI combined with wet-lab validation. The company went public via a SPAC in 2021 and has iterated its Integrated Drug Creation platform, reporting rapid generation of functional antibodies. It announced partnerships with major companies including AstraZeneca and Merck for antibody and enzyme design. Today Absci's models design candidate antibodies in silico that are synthesized and tested in weeks, targeting oncology, inflammation, and other therapeutic areas.

name: Iambic Therapeutics
short_description: Generative chemistry platform tuned for clinical relevance.
why_relevant: Fast-tracked AI-designed oncology candidates into the clinic.
history: Founded in 2019, Iambic Therapeutics develops generative chemistry models calibrated for clinical relevance, with physics-grounded neural networks that approach DFT accuracy. It raised substantial venture funding and quickly advanced lead AI-designed oncology candidates into Phase 1 clinical trials. The company later expanded into new headquarters in the San Francisco Bay Area and broadened its platform across therapeutic areas. Today Iambic continues to fast-track computationally designed drugs through the clinic while building collaborations across biopharma.

name: XtalPi
short_description: Combines quantum chemistry and AI for computational drug discovery.
why_relevant: Industrial-scale crystal and drug prediction at GMP quality.
history: Founded in 2014, XtalPi combines quantum chemistry, physics-based prediction, and machine learning for drug discovery. The company operates one of the world's largest computational crystal- and drug-prediction platforms and expanded into integrated drug-discovery services. It formed strategic alliances with Chinese and global pharma, including collaborations to industrialize physics-driven R&D. XtalPi continues to scale its prediction engines to GMP-grade quality for crystallization and drug development.

name: Schrodinger
short_description: Physics-based and ML software for molecular discovery.
why_relevant: The standard platform modern drug discovery teams compute on.
history: Founded in 1990, Schrodinger built physics-based computational platforms that many drug discovery teams rely on for molecular design. The company went public on the Nasdaq in 2020 and advanced free-energy perturbation methods like FEP+ for quantitative drug design. It serves major pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and incubates internal programs through its own research arm. Today Schrodinger remains the standard computational platform that modern drug discovery organizations compute on.

name: Basecamp Research
short_description: Builds the world's largest biodiversity genomic dataset for protein AI.
why_relevant: Feeds frontier protein models with legally clear biological data.
history: Founded in 2020 in London, Basecamp Research builds the world's largest biodiversity genomic dataset, collected through global field expeditions with partner institutions. The company combines metagenomics with protein foundation models, providing biologically diverse and legally clear data for frontier AI. It raised tens of millions of dollars and partnered with Genentech in 2024 to develop foundation models for protein design. Today Basecamp feeds next-generation protein AI with real-world biological data at unprecedented scale.

name: Arzeda
short_description: Designs industrial enzymes from scratch with computational methods.
why_relevant: De novo enzymes replacing petrochemical processes in industry.
history: Founded in 2008 in the Seattle area, Arzeda designs industrial enzymes from scratch using computational methods. The company raised strategic funding, including support from Breakthrough Energy Ventures and U.S. government programs, to build proteins that replace petrochemical processes. Arzeda has demonstrated its designed enzymes across pilot and commercial processes, including high-value industrial uses. Today it focuses on de novo enzyme design that upgrades biological manufacturing for agriculture, materials, and chemicals.

name: Nuclera
short_description: Desktop tool that prints the proteins you need on demand.
why_relevant: Frees researchers from expression waits in protein discovery.
history: Founded in 2013 in the UK, Nuclera developed a desktop benchtop instrument that rapidly prints proteins on demand using cell-free expression and inkjet technology. The company raised tens of millions of dollars, including a Series B in 2024, making protein discovery faster for research teams. Its eProtein Discovery system condenses days of expression work into hours and prints functional proteins for screening. Today Nuclera is bringing protein bioprinting to laboratories worldwide.

name: Skyhawk Therapeutics
short_description: Small molecules that tune RNA splicing to treat genetic disease.
why_relevant: First-in-class oral splicing modulators for CNS and cancer targets.
history: Founded in 2016, Skyhawk Therapeutics develops first-in-class small molecules that modulate RNA splicing to treat genetic disease. The company raised significant funding, including a financing in 2023 co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, and formed drug-discovery alliances with major pharma. Its platform targets neurological, oncology, and rare-disease programs, with oral splicing modulators advancing toward the clinic. Today Skyhawk continues to expand its RNA-splicing platform across multiple therapeutic areas.

name: Deep Genomics
short_description: Predicts how DNA variants cause disease to design therapies.
why_relevant: Uses learned variant-effect models as the discovery engine.
history: Founded in 2015 by machine-learning pioneer Brendan Frey, Deep Genomics built AI models that predict precisely how DNA variants cause disease. The company secured financing from investors including Radical Ventures and Neo as it applied its variant-effect engine to develop oligonucleotide therapies for genetic disease. It has formed collaborations with biopharma across neurological, metabolic, and rare conditions. Today Deep Genomics uses its learned variant-effect models as the engine for its discovery pipeline.
